guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul (Joe Perry has a Bone Yard signature) / Brad Whitford Gibson Les Paul
models: Gibson Les Paul (Joe Perry has a Bone Yard signature)
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: Joe Perry is famously a Gibson Les Paul player (Billie Perry / Boneyard signatures), Brad Whitford also plays Les Pauls.
guitar.notes: Original was reasonable; refined to emphasize Les Paul as primary for both, dropped Strat mention as less central.

tone.target: tight crunchy hard-rock riff with bright upper-mid bite
tone.profile: tight crunchy hard-rock riff with bright upper-mid bite
tone.summary: A tight, bright hard rock tone achieved with a pre-drive boost and the UK 45 amp model, paired with a classic British cab for maximum upper-mid bite and rhythmic chug.
corrections: avoid Tube Screamer as main flavor

rig.name: Aerosmith - Walk This Way - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up pick noise and hum for tight riffing.
Provide the necessary snappy attack and mid-range punch without sounding like a full Tube Screamer.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used as a general boost/overdrive to achieve the 'light boost only' requirement, avoiding specific TS models.

alternatives.reason: A slightly more aggressive alternative if more grit is needed.

blocks.purpose: Add slight grind and controlled crunch without excessive fuzz or metal gain.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style is used sparingly to add grit/crunch, keeping the overall tone focused on upper mids rather than heavy distortion.

alternatives.reason: A more general option if the crunch needs to be less aggressive.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Plexi/Marshall style required for classic hard rock punch and bright upper-mids.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and complement the UK 45 amp model.
Sculpt the tone to emphasize upper-mids and bite, fulfilling the 'bright bite' requirement.
Optional subtle thickening for sustained notes (kept off for tight riffing).
blocks.gap: The Chorus is generally avoided for very dry, rhythmic chugging, but included as a potential texture module.

alternatives.reason: If the riff needs more movement rather than thickness.

blocks.purpose: Used for fills or transitions, kept off during the main riffing section to maintain tightness.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet simulation to enhance upper-mid bite and realism for hard rock riffing.

proposals.reason: Enhance upper-mid bite and punch for hard rock riffing.
